items.title: 66960_Gil Evans oral history interview
items.q: I haven't analysed the parts of the album very good that I like very much so, the parts of Webern that I like very much. Some of them may be done by that strictly, but they were both students of Schoenberg.

ctx.x: Now at the beginning of this, Schoenberg is teaching the twelve tone saying that if you play the twelve tones and you select the order of the twelve tones you want and you never repeat it. And so you go through the whole twelve tones. You are not allowed to go back to any of those twelve notes. You work all twelve of them in a combination somehow and then you go back to the first one and do that and go on again, you know. So that's very strict and not too easy to do and it hasn't been proved that the results are…

I haven't analysed the parts of the album very good that I like very much so, the parts of Webern that I like very much. Some of them may be done by that strictly, but they were both students of Schoenberg. And they did, the applied the twelve tone thing to their writing. In a freer manner, they would go from that?) in both regular tradition writing into that and back again, wouldn't have to play all twelve tones.
